subject.title: Anthropic setup-token onboarding path has multiple failure modes (docs gap, credential propagation, multi-agent sync)

question: Should Anthropic setup-token onboarding copy static token profiles into sibling agent stores, or should OpenClaw keep main-store read-through and focus this issue on setup-token guidance, validation, and docs?
rationale: The choice changes where Anthropic tokens are persisted and whether OpenClaw silently expands credential availability across agents, which is a security and upgrade boundary rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Prefer inheritance plus validation
options.body: Keep credentials in the selected/default store, improve setup-token instructions and post-write/status validation, and avoid new automatic secret copying by default.

options.title: Approve static-token sibling sync
options.body: Allow setup-token/paste-token to copy portable static token profiles into sibling agent stores with tests and security-facing docs.

options.title: Close after current behavior proof
options.body: If maintainers decide SQLite read-through fully covers this path, close this issue and request a fresh live repro for any remaining setup-token failure.

recommendation.title: Prefer inheritance plus validation
recommendation.body: Keep credentials in the selected/default store, improve setup-token instructions and post-write/status validation, and avoid new automatic secret copying by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history for auth storage, read-through semantics, and Anthropic setup-token behavior points to steipete.
